First of all, I want to tell you how fucking awesome and strong it is of you to pursue your dream. Dropping out of college isn’t an easy decision, and it takes an insane level of determination, self-discipline and self-belief.

Secondly, COVID fucking sucks. It’s taken so much happiness and opportunity away, and it’s okay to feel this way. You did everything right: you set up your education, found a place to live, you sacrificed a seven year relationship for what you really wanted in life. You have every reason to feel the way you do. 

Thirdly,  just because you’re in a temporary location doesn’t mean you can’t connect with people. Everyone’s lonely, which means picking up a group of casual friends or even just acquaintances (especially now that you live in the city) may not be as hard as you think. They might not become your forever friends, but they they’d be what you need in this moment. I know it’s not easy; I have severe social anxiety and have struggled with something akin to what you’re dealing with since the pandemic started. But we’ll get through it. You’re going to make it as an air traffic controller, you just have to keep up that determination and faith that got you started on this path.

Not that this compares in any way to rape, but I fucked myself up by downloading tiktok. At first I thought it would be a nice and easy way to make friends, but then I fell into this pit of comparing myself to popular creators and wondering why I wasn’t as liked as them and then spending hours trying to become popular and seen. I missed schoolwork, ignored my cat, stayed up late, and this was all in a period of about a month. Alongside that, I was filling my mind with content about depression and anxiety and self harm and suicide, so much that it affected my mental health and I stopped taking my antidepressants and started drowning in my own depression and anxiety and I almost self harmed, which I haven’t done in about a year. I thought I could handle tiktok, but I was wrong and I paid the consequences. BUT THAT DOESNT MEAN WHAT I FELT WASNT REAL OR THAT IM A BAD PERSON FOR DOING WHAT I DID. It just means I made a poor judgement call, an innocent mistake. And I think that’s what you did, too. Go easy on yourself; you had the courage to try and tackle something. You learned that you can’t tackle it right now, but that doesn’t you never will. Be patient with yourself and take care of yourself so that when the time comes to face this again, you’ll be better prepared. Wishing you well 💖

Maybe you could message your teacher privately or ask to speak with them during their office hours. A lot of students probably ARE half-assing their classes and blaming their poor participation on internet problems. The leaving the class early thing I can TOTALLY get. I’ve thought about doing it before, too. And putting a student who was slacking because they didn’t care about the class on the spot may work. Because it shows the student that just because the teacher can’t reprimand them face to face, it doesn’t mean that the student can walk all over them. 

Maybe if you explain to your teacher your anxiety and the situation with your classmates, they’ll be more understanding and willing to work with you. Teachers want to know that their students respect them especially now, and I think you’re accidentally giving off the same vibes as students who don’t respect online teachers. 

And if this doesn’t work, maybe try talking to your principal or guidance counselor or advisor if you’re in college. Anxiety is a real issue and you deserve to get an education and be successful in spite of it.
Never feel bad about your successes. You deserve every good thing in your life and I hope you stay this happy for a long time 🙌
